purpose: Every link between RealityEngine entities, its protocol, its transport status today and the issue that brings it to the profile (RealityEngine_CI#668, #725). status: plaintext | tls (encrypted, profile compliance not yet verified) | compliant (verified against the profile by the probe stage, #728) | unverified (not yet checked). mtls is true only when the probe has verified both ends present install-CA certificates. A link may carry a `deficiency` only by owner decision: what falls short of the profile, what compensates, the remedy, and `allows`, the exact status or mtls value it permits. The release gate reports such a link instead of failing on it, within what `allows` permits.

deficiency.what: Qdrant v1.20 (rustls) cannot be restricted: with client-certificate verification on it still accepts TLS 1.2 and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and offers no post-quantum group, so the server side can never be verified compliant.

deficiency.remedy: A Qdrant setting that restricts protocol versions and suites; then this deficiency is removed.

links.note: Ollama serves no TLS (0.40.13; its FAQ offers only a reverse proxy). links.to: Ollama on the Mac (host.docker.internal:11434 from containers, 127.0.0.1:11434 from the gateway)
links.note: A release install has no TLS front for Ollama: the front (localAIStack scripts/ollama_tls_front.py) runs on the host on the dev lanes, and a release Mac cannot be assumed to have Python.

deficiency.what: In a release install every Ollama client reaches the Mac's Ollama over plain http: from containers through Docker Desktop's host gateway, from the native gateway on loopback.
deficiency.compensation: Ollama binds 127.0.0.1 only, so nothing off the Mac reaches it; the traffic carries prompts and completions for local models, no credentials.
deficiency.remedy: A host-side TLS front the release can run (the front ported to Node, which the release already requires), or native TLS in Ollama; then this link leaves the list.

links.note: Verified by hand 2026-11-08 against OpenClaw 2026.10.8 with a throwaway lane CA (localOpenClawStack#93): the native gateway serves HTTPS/WSS with the lane certificate; TLS 1.3, X25519MLKEM768, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384; AES-128, P-256, TLS 1.2 and plaintext refused. The PEs record wss://127.0.0.1:18789 on the lane; the ACP adapter (scripts/openclaw-acp-adapter.mjs) still has to move to the lane CA. Not `compliant` until the probe (#728) records it. Live 2026-11-08 (run tls-lane-20261108c, RE_TLS=on, native universe with OpenClaw on): verify-deployment.sh passed on the lane (TLS health, token 401, 0-critical security audit, agents read from all three engines over mTLS); the listener negotiated X25519MLKEM768 + AES-256-GCM and refused TLS 1.2, AES-128, P-256 and plaintext.

deficiency.what: OpenClaw 2026.10.8's gateway TLS server cannot require client certificates (no requestCert; gateway.tls.caPath is a trust chain only), so its inbound links are TLS 1.3 without mTLS.
deficiency.compensation: Every call needs the gateway bearer token (verify-deployment.sh checks a call without it gets 401); the gateway binds loopback only; the listener is held to the full profile by scripts/lib/lane-tls-preload.cjs.
deficiency.remedy: mTLS once OpenClaw can require client certificates.

links.note: On the native lane with RE_TLS=on (docker-compose.observability-tls.yml, startUniverse.sh obs_compose; #730): Loki serves TLS 1.3 requiring a lane client certificate; Promtail verifies it against the lane CA as loki and presents its own. Not `compliant` until the probe (#728) records it. Live 2026-11-08 (run tls-lane-20261108e, RE_TLS=on): Loki ready over mTLS; logs from the engines arrived (3 streams); Loki negotiated X25519MLKEM768 and refused TLS 1.2, no certificate and plaintext (400).

deficiency.what: Loki (and its client Promtail) is Go: crypto/tls does not let TLS 1.3 cipher suites be configured, so TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 stays negotiable (Go-to-Go links negotiate it), and P-256 is accepted (an explicit curve list would drop X25519MLKEM768). TLS 1.3-only and mTLS are enforced.
deficiency.compensation: AES-128-GCM is AEAD; every link is TLS 1.3 with a lane client certificate required (Grafana's browser port: server TLS); the services are on the compose network and loopback-bound host ports; Loki 3.5.10 and Prometheus v3.15.1 (Go 1.25+) offer X25519MLKEM768.
deficiency.remedy: Go adds TLS 1.3 suite configuration, or the services move behind an OpenSSL front.
